newsitem.title: UK: James and Alice top Thomas and Charlotte.
newsitem.headline: James and Alice top Thomas and Charlotte.

text.p: James and Alice are this year's most popular names for British babies, ousting Thomas and Charlotte from the top spot, according to a survey of 4,000 birth announcements published in The Times.
The National Health Service's central register currently shows Jack and Jessica are the favourite names for babies up and down Britain.
But The Times, somewhat sniffily, said parents who place birth notices in its columns are ahead of the game.
"The names they choose do not reflect overall trends, but their choices tend to gain wider popularity a few years later," the newspaper said in its Saturday edition.
In its list, Jack ranked just eleventh and Jessica languished in twentieth spot.
Thomas, William and Alexander were the most popular names after James. Alice led the girls' rankings ahead of Olivia, Emily and Sophie.
